facts.statement: The genus Leurospondylus was described by Brown in 1913.
The specific name *ultimus* means 'last' because the genus represented the latest known fossil plesiosaur at the time of its description in 1913.
facts.quote: It was so named because this genus was the latest known occurrence of a fossil plesiosaur when it was described in 1913.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Leurospondylus ultimus was a juvenile animal.
facts.quote: The holotype of L. ultimus was a juvenile.

facts.statement: Samuel Paul Welles noted that the vertebrae resemble those of pliosaurs while the shoulder bones resemble those of elasmosaurids, making family classification difficult.
facts.quote: Samuel Paul Welles noted that the vertebrae are short and similar to those of pliosaurs, while the scapulae and coracoids bear resemblance to those of elasmosaurids, thus making it difficult to determine to which family it belongs.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the Leurospondylus specimen is a juvenile of a known species or belongs to an unrecognized taxonomic group.
facts.quote: There is some speculation that the Leurospondylus specimen is either a juvenile of a known species, or in its own, unrecognized taxonomic group.

facts.statement: Leurospondylus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
Leurospondylus lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype was found in the brackish Edmonton beds of the present-day Red Deer River.
facts.quote: The holotype was found in the brackish paleoenvironment represented by the Edmonton beds located on the present-day Red Deer River.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: This area is part of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: It is unknown whether Leurospondylus grew up and left the freshwater ecosystem or remained there as an adult.
facts.quote: However, some plesiosaurs spent their adult lives in fresh water also; whether Leurospondylus grew up and then left, or grew up and stayed in a fresh water ecosystem has not been determined.

facts.statement: The family of Leurospondylus is disputed, though it is suggested to belong to Elasmosauridae.
facts.quote: Leurospondylus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Canada whose family is currently disputed, but is suggested to be Elasmosauridae.

facts.statement: Some sources suggest Leurospondylus belongs to the family Plesiosauridae, though this is disputed.
facts.quote: Leurospondylus es un género de plesiosaurio cuya familia está actualmente en disputa, pero se sugiere que sea un Plesiosauridae.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Leurospondylus as Elasmosauridae.
